{{ElectionsPA}}
The '''2024 United States Senate election in Pennsylvania''' was held on November 5, 2024, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Pennsylvania]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] businessman [[Dave McCormick]] won his first term in office, defeating [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] three-term incumbent [[Bob Casey Jr.]] in what was considered a major [[Upset (competition)|upset]].<ref name="Katie Glueck-2024">{{Cite news |last=Glueck |first=Katie |date=2024-11-21 |title=David McCormick Defeats Senator Bob Casey in Pennsylvania |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/11/21/us/politics/bob-casey-david-mccormick-pennsylvania-senate.html |access-date=2026-03-16 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Most predictions gave Casey a slight advantage, and he led in most polls. Along with [[Sherrod Brown]] in [[2024 United States Senate election in Ohio|Ohio]] and [[Jon Tester]] in [[2024 United States Senate election in Montana|Montana]], Casey was one of three incumbent senators to lose re-election in 2024, all of whom were Democrats first elected in [[2006 United States Senate elections|2006]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2024/12/14/bob-casey-trump-pennsylvania/|title=Why Bob Casey couldn't overcome the 'Trump wave' in Pennsylvania|date=December 14, 2024|newspaper=The Washington Post|quote=The three-term senator lost amid Trump's grip on rural voters and sagging turnout around metropolitan areas like Philadelphia.|first1=Paul|last1=Kane|access-date=December 14, 2024}}</ref>
 
The primary election took place on April 23, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=www.ncsl.org |archive-date=August 17, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230817074608/https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |url-status=live }}</ref> The election was considered essential for Democrats' chances to retain their majority in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pathe |first=Simone |date=2024-07-20 |title=The 10 Senate seats most likely to flip in 2024 {{!}} CNN Politics |url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/07/20/politics/senate-race-rankings-july-2024 |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref> The [[Associated Press]] and [[Fox News]] declared McCormick the winner on November 7,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Levy |first=Marc |date=2024-11-07 |title=Republican David McCormick flips pivotal Pennsylvania Senate seat, ousts Bob Casey |url=https://apnews.com/article/pennsylvania-senate-2024-election-david-mccormick-casey-866a8712dea0b52b5d8d6b4844968b53 |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> while [[Decision Desk HQ]] called the race for McCormick on November 14.<ref>{{cite web |title=2024 Pennsylvania US Senate |url=https://votes.decisiondeskhq.com/races/2024-11-05/pennsylvania-us-senate-general-election |website=DDHQ Votes |access-date=May 7, 2026 |date=November 14, 2024}}</ref> [[CNN]], [[NBC]], [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]], and [[CBS]] all called the race for McCormick on November 21; Casey conceded the race later that day,<ref name="Emily Rose Grassi-2024">{{Cite web |last=Levy |first=Marc |date=2024-11-21 |title=Democrat Bob Casey concedes to Republican David McCormick in Pennsylvania Senate contest |url=https://apnews.com/article/casey-mccormick-pennsylvania-senate-71f58415fb1e1fd7f00ef617808a7c4c |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> halted a recount and confirmed the result.<ref>{{cite news |work=CNN Politics |title=Senate race in Pennsylvania heads to a recount |date=November 13, 2024 |access-date=November 14, 2024 |archive-date=November 14, 2024 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241114054613/https://edition.cnn.com/2024/11/13/politics/pennsylvania-senate-race-heads-to-a-recount/index.html |first1=Ethan |last1=Cohen |last2=Hudspeth Blackburn |first2=Piper |first3=Morgan |last3=Rimmer |last4=Pathe |first4=Simone |last5=Krieg |first5=Gregory |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2024/11/13/politics/pennsylvania-senate-race-heads-to-a-recount/index.html}}</ref>

This was Pennsylvania's closest US Senate election since the passage of the [[Seventeenth Amendment to the United States Constitution|Seventeenth Amendment]], as well as the closest Senate election of the 2024 cycle. McCormick was the only Republican challenger to win in a state flipped by Trump in the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 presidential election]]. The other three Republican Senate gains were in states Trump had won in all three of his runs. With Democrats flipping the other Senate seat [[2022 United States Senate election in Pennsylvania|two years earlier]], this was the first time since the [[2012 United States Senate election in Indiana|2012 Senate election in Indiana]] where the opposite party flipped a seat after losing one in the previous cycle.

This was Casey's first general election loss of his political career, and the second counting Casey's primary election loss in [[2002 Pennsylvania gubernatorial election|2002]]. This election made Pennsylvania one of several states to have a younger [[senior senator]] ([[John Fetterman]]) and an older [[junior senator]] (McCormick). McCormick was sworn in on January 3, 2025.

{{toclimit|3}}

== Background ==
Pennsylvania is considered to be a [[Red states and blue states|purple]] state at the federal level, especially since in the [[2020 United States presidential election in Pennsylvania|2020 presidential election]], [[Joe Biden]] carried Pennsylvania by about 1.2 percentage points. Democrats had controlled both U.S. Senate seats, the governorship, a majority of its [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House]] [[Pennsylvania's congressional delegations|delegation]], and the [[Pennsylvania House of Representatives]]. The last time Republicans won a [[U.S. Senate]] seat in Pennsylvania was in [[2016 United States Senate election in Pennsylvania|2016]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pennsylvania 2020 presidential election results |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2020/results/state/pennsylvania/president |access-date=March 19, 2023 |website=[[CNN]] |language=en |archive-date=October 8, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241008060734/https://www.cnn.com/election/2020/results/state/pennsylvania/president |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Pennsylvania Governor Midterm Election Results and Maps 2022 |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2022/results/pennsylvania/governor |access-date=March 19, 2023 |website=[[CNN]] |language=en |archive-date=October 7, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007104826/https://www.cnn.com/election/2022/results/pennsylvania/governor |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Narea |first=Nicole |date=February 8, 2023 |title=Democrats in Pennsylvania just won the 2022 midterms. Again. |url=https://www.vox.com/policy-and-politics/2023/2/8/23591602/pennsylvania-house-democrats-win-special-election-majority |access-date=March 19, 2023 |website=[[Vox (website)|Vox]] |language=en |archive-date=September 29, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230929040528/https://www.vox.com/policy-and-politics/2023/2/8/23591602/pennsylvania-house-democrats-win-special-election-majority |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=United States Senate election in Pennsylvania, 2016 |url=https://ballotpedia.org/United_States_Senate_election_in_Pennsylvania,_2016 |access-date=March 19, 2023 |website=[[Ballotpedia]] |language=en}}</ref>

Senator Bob Casey Jr. was first elected in the blue wave of [[2006 United States Senate election in Pennsylvania|2006]], defeating then-incumbent Senator [[Rick Santorum]] by about 17 percentage points. He was re-elected in [[2012 United States Senate election in Pennsylvania|2012]] by 9 percentage points (when he ran ahead of Obama by almost 4 points) and in the blue wave of [[2018 United States Senate election in Pennsylvania|2018]] by 13 percentage points.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pennsylvania Senate 2006 Race |url=https://www.opensecrets.org/races/summary?cycle=2006&id=PAS2 |access-date=March 19, 2023 |website=[[OpenSecrets]] |language=en |archive-date=September 27, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230927025427/https://www.opensecrets.org/races/summary?cycle=2006&id=PAS2 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Pennsylvania |language=en-US |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/elections/2012/results/states/pennsylvania.html |access-date=March 19, 2023 |issn=0362-4331 |archive-date=October 9, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241009182606/https://www.nytimes.com/elections/2012/results/states/pennsylvania.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Pennsylvania Senate Election Results 2018: Live Midterm Map by County & Analysis |url=https://www.politico.com/election-results/2018/pennsylvania/senate/ |access-date=March 19, 2023 |website=[[Politico]] |date=November 7, 2018 |language=en |archive-date=September 11, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240911021016/https://www.politico.com/election-results/2018/pennsylvania/senate/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Given these three decisive victories, Casey's fourth term appeared inevitable for much of the race. However, tightening polls in the final weeks indicated a closer contest, even as Casey was largely considered the favorite to win.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hudson |first=Lee |title=Bob Casey running for Senate reelection |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2023/04/10/bob-casey-senate-reelection-00091186 |access-date=April 19, 2023 |website=[[Politico]] |date=April 10, 2023 |language=en |archive-date=June 30, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230630230709/https://www.politico.com/news/2023/04/10/bob-casey-senate-reelection-00091186 |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Analysis ==
In Pennsylvania, a statewide [[Election recount|recount]] is triggered under state law if the margin falls within 0.5% of the total vote. Preliminary results for the election reached this threshold on November 13, 2024, with McCormick at 48.9% leading Casey's 48.6%, as outstanding ballots continued to be counted across the state. [[Secretary of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania|Secretary of the Commonwealth]] [[Al Schmidt]] officially ordered the recount later that evening, with Casey declining to concede.<ref>{{cite news |title=Recount triggered in Pennsylvania Senate race as McCormick heads to D.C., Casey declines to concede |first=Dan |last=Snyder |work=[[CBS News]] |date=November 13, 2024 |access-date=November 13, 2024 |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/philadelphia/news/pennsylvania-senate-casey-mccormick-recount/}}</ref> The deadline for the counties to begin their recounts is on November 20, the third Wednesday after the election according to state law, however, counties can start their recounts as early as November 18, with all counties required to submit their results to the [[Pennsylvania Department of State|Department of State]] by noon on November 26 as the results must be reported by the Secretary of the Commonwealth by noon on November 27.<ref>{{cite news |title=Pennsylvania's Senate race is going to a recount. How will it work? |first1=Katie |last1=Bernard |first2=Jonathan |last2=Lai |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=November 14, 2024 |access-date=November 14, 2024 |url=https://www.inquirer.com/politics/election/pennsylvania-senate-recount-casey-mccormick-20241114.html}}</ref> Additionally, the counties must use different machines for the recount than were used on Election Day.<ref>{{cite web |title=Recount starts in Pennsylvania US Senate race between Casey, McCormick |url=https://www.wgal.com/article/pennsylvania-us-senate-race-casey-vs-mccormick-recount-update/62936018 |website=[[WGAL]] |access-date=18 November 2024}}</ref>

On Monday, November 18, following a series of challenges and disputes, the Pennsylvania Supreme Court directed all of the state's county election officials not to count certain mail-in ballots which  arrived on time yet lacked a correct handwritten date on the return envelope.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lo Wang |first1=Hansi |title=Pennsylvania's high court sides with Republicans on misdated mail ballots |url=https://www.npr.org/2024/11/18/nx-s1-5195524/pennsylvania-election-ballots-senate-recount |website=[[NPR]] |date=November 18, 2024 |access-date=19 November 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=LEVY |first1=MARC |title=Pennsylvania's high court orders counties not to count disputed ballots in US Senate race |url=https://apnews.com/article/casey-mccormick-pennsylvania-senate-court-recount-b6c9ee8faac20d6272a54900e2d570e7 |website=[[Associated Press|AP]] |date=November 18, 2024 |access-date=19 November 2024}}</ref>

The last instance of a statewide recount being held was for the [[2022 United States Senate election in Pennsylvania#Republican primary|2022 Republican primary]] for Pennsylvania's Class 3 Senate seat, of which McCormick was also a candidate. Conversely to his stance in the 2024 general election, he unsuccessfully sued to have undated mail-in ballots counted. After completion of the recount he would concede to [[Mehmet Oz]], with the final results expanding Oz's margin by 49 votes.<ref>{{cite news |title=Elections 101: Everything you need to know about election recounts in Pennsylvania |first=Carter |last=Walker |work=[[Spotlight PA]] |date=June 13, 2024 |access-date=November 14, 2024 |url=https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2024/06/pennsylvania-election-recounts-explainer-donald-trump-joe-biden/}}</ref>

McCormick benefitted from the presence of former President Donald Trump on the ballot, who carried the state over Vice President Harris by just over 120,000 votes (for a margin of roughly 1.7%) in the concurrent presidential election. Indeed, McCormick cleared 60% in most counties in the state’s less-populated interior and even 70% in many. Unlike in Ohio and Montana, however, McCormick had to seek support beyond the Trump base as he was running in a swing state. Casey and Trump both won Bucks, Erie, and Monroe Counties. McCormick campaigned with [[Nikki Haley]] in the suburbs of Pittsburgh and [[Philadelphia Main Line|Philadelphia]], aiming to appeal to voters uneasy about Trump by positioning himself as a more establishment candidate. Casey aired ads in late October to highlight his votes with the Trump administration, while McCormick tied Casey to Harris, highlighting his votes with the Biden administration. 

However, both candidates received fewer votes than their respective parties’ presidential candidates in the concurrent [[2024 United States presidential election in Pennsylvania|2024 presidential election]]. Senator McCormick received about 144,000 fewer votes than President Trump, while Senator Casey received almost 39,000 fewer votes than Vice President Harris. Although, McCormick overperformed Trump's margins in the Philadelphia suburban counties of Chester, Delaware, and Montgomery.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-31 |title=David McCormick campaigns with Nikki Haley in Senate-race push for moderate voters in Western Pa. |url=https://www.wesa.fm/politics-government/2024-10-31/david-mccormick-campaigns-with-nikki-haley-in-senate-race-push-for-moderate-voters-in-western-pa |access-date=2024-12-02 |website=90.5 WESA |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Walsh |first=Sean Collins |date=2024-11-09 |title=Trump, messaging, and money: How Dave McCormick unseated Bob Casey in Pennsylvania's Senate race |url=https://www.inquirer.com/politics/philadelphia/how-dave-mccormick-won-us-senate-race-20241109.html |access-date=2024-12-02 |website=www.inquirer.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Walsh |first=Sean Collins |date=2024-11-09 |title=Haley campaigns for McCormick in Philly and Pittsburgh suburbs |url=https://penncapital-star.com/campaigns-elections/pennsylvania-nikki-haley-campaigns-for-mccormick-in-philly-and-pittsburgh-suburbs/ |access-date=2024-12-02 |website=www.penncapital-star.com |language=en}}</ref>
